a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Vinorelbine, a large complex indole-containing natural product, has absolute oral bioavailability of 43 ± 14% (close to 40% by AUCinf) in fasted patients, supporting that a complex macrocyclic indole-containing molecule of similar size can exceed the 20% threshold.
Naldemedine, another complex polycyclic natural-product-derived molecule, has estimated absolute oral bioavailability of 20–56%, consistent with F ≥ 20%.
The only near-threshold L1 value, maraviroc F = 0.24 (24%), is still above the 20% threshold; no L1 record affirmatively supports F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule or a close structural analog.
No matched oral vs IV exposure data for the query.
Transfer from vinorelbine and naldemedine is qualitative; structural similarity is limited.
No formulation, dose, or prandial-state data for the query.
The physicochemical prior is mixed/unclear and does not affirmatively support either class.
content.decision_summary: All L1 gold-context records are at or above the 20% threshold (e.g., vinorelbine ~40%, naldemedine 20–56%, maraviroc 24%), and none affirmatively supports F < 20%. The most structurally relevant context, vinorelbine, shows that a large complex indole-containing natural product can have ~40% absolute oral bioavailability. The mixed physicochemical prior does not provide affirmative low-F evidence. Therefore predict high with moderate confidence.
